note: Copies attacker-controlled bytes into the mutable request buffer used by the parser.
Routes the copied input into header parsing after method and path parsing succeed.
The parser stores two pointers per header without a sufficient bound check before the writes; the safety obligation is that the header pointer count stays below the fixed array capacity.

code: if (n_headers > N_HEADER_START || p >= buffer_end) { helper->n_header_start = 0; return false; }
note: The capacity check happens after the writes, so it cannot prevent overflow once too many CR-delimited headers are present.
When the input contains more than 64 header delimiters, these writes run past the 64-element header_start array, causing the global-buffer-overflow write.
